title: Regional + Tier Fallback Harmonizer: spec and validator for mixed-policy configs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: our current routing DSL allows independently authored region selectors, tier rules, and fallback model variants which leads to ambiguous precedence, accidental cycles (tier A -> fallback B -> region constraint mismatch), and surprising runtime fallthroughs. This ticket defines a harmonizer stage that normalizes mixed-policy configs into a deterministic canonical manifest and a validator library that rejects unsafe constructs before rollout.

Goals: produce a clear specification for canonicalization, implement a fast validator (library + CLI) used by the Console and CI, add a migration shim that rewrites legacy rules into the new canonical form where possible, and create a staged rollout plan that minimizes customer impact. The harmonizer will also emit provenance annotations for each effective rule (original source, transformation applied) to aid audits and debuggability.
acceptance_criteria: Spec: a single document that defines canonical manifest format, precedence rules (region > tier > model-variant unless explicit override), and forbidden constructs; reviewed and approved by PM and Security
Validator: a library (Go and TS bindings) that performs schema + semantic validation and returns structured errors with suggested fixes; unit coverage >= 90%
CLI/CI: a command-line tool and CI hook that fail merges for configs that contain cycles, unreachable fallbacks, or cross-region variant violations
Migration shim: an opt-in transformer that rewrites >80% of legacy configs into canonical form with a generated migration report per-customer
Observability: harmonizer emits telemetry for transformed rules (count, transform-type) and validation failures (reason codes) to Console dashboards
Rollout: canary rollout executed for 5 internal teams for two weeks with no customer-facing errors recorded; rollback procedure documented
test_plan: Unit: validator rule-level tests for precedence, cycle detection, and unreachable fallback detection
Integration: end-to-end tests that run config -> harmonizer -> runtime simulation and assert identical effective routing decisions as golden manifests
Property-based: random policy generator to fuzz for invariants (no cycles, region-compatibility)
Regression: import test-suite from customers with known problematic configs (internal dataset)
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (internal): deploy validator to staging Console and add CI gate for internal repos (1 week)
Stage 1 (canary): opt-in canary with 5 internal product teams, enable migration shim with verbose logging (2 weeks)
Stage 2 (gradual): enable validator for new rules only (reject) and continue offering migration shim as a rewrite tool (4 weeks)
Stage 3 (enforce): enable validator in production CI for all infra-as-code repos; migrate existing customers with >80% compatible configs and schedule manual review for the rest
comments: 2025-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Drafted initial problem statement; scoped harmonizer to normalization + validator + optional migration shim. Assigned to Marcus.

2025-02-18 - Marcus Nguyen: Spike completed — proved cycle detection algorithm with complexity O(E+V) using Tarjan SCC; prototype validator implemented in Go and exposes JSON error codes. Link to spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/1312

2025-02-25 - Design review: PM (Ravi Singh) requested explicit provenance annotations on canonical manifests; Security (Lina Zhao) requested an audit log schema. Action: add lambda-friendly audit payload and make provenance a first-class field.

2025-03-03 - Engineering sync: decided precedence model: explicit overrides trump derived fallbacks; region-scoped fallbacks must be compatible with region selectors or validator rejects. Trade-off: tighter validation will reject some legacy configs — mitigated with migration shim and an 'escape hatch' flag for enterprise support.

2025-03-08 - PR feedback from reviewers: increase test coverage for multi-tenant manifest merge cases; add synthetic customer config corpus. PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/1356
2025-03-12 - Marcus Nguyen: Validator alpha deployed to staging Console; telemetry emitted to routing.harmonizer.* metrics. Preparing canary rollout notes and runbook.
2025-03-12 - QA (Elena Gomez): Found edge case where variant aliasing caused unreachable fallback in multi-tier rules; created sub-issue ENG-87911 to fix alias resolution in migrator.
notes: Consider adding a lightweight protobuf representation for canonical manifests to keep Console <-> runtime payloads compact.
We should coordinate with Dedicated infra team to ensure validator runs before capacity reservations to avoid dead-lettering requests.
Keep migration shim opt-in by default for enterprise customers with custom automation; provide a dry-run report for every transformation.
